resources.string: The size of message text in conversations. The rest of Khandaq follows the text size set on the phone.
Asks the keyboard not to learn from what you type in messages. Whether it does is up to the keyboard.
The chat list, conversations and calls stay out of screenshots and screen recordings, and recent apps show them blank.
A conversation shows this many messages at a time, and earlier ones are a tap away. 0 shows them all at once, which can be slow in a long conversation.
In group conversations, a line says when someone joins, leaves or changes their name.
In a group with an IRC bridge, the messages it relays from this name are hidden. Leave empty if you do not use one.
Another name to hide, or leave empty.
Pictures up to 12 MB download without asking.
Videos up to 200 MB download without asking.
Any file up to 200 MB downloads without asking, which takes storage and data.
Lets you send photos and files to a conversation from the Share menu of another app.
A received file opens straight in another app, without being saved to the phone first. A harmful app could then also read other files that Khandaq keeps encrypted.
In a voice call the screen turns off while the phone is at your ear. If it then does not come back on, turn this off: the screen only goes blank instead.
Raises a quiet voice automatically in calls. If calls sound distorted, turn this off.
Makes your voice louder in calls when your microphone is quiet. 1 means no boost.
For a microphone that is too loud: the boost above then makes your voice quieter instead of louder.
Filters background noise, such as traffic or a fan, out of your voice in calls. Uses a little more battery.
Higher quality sounds clearer and uses more data. Applies from the next call.
If your video comes out in the wrong colours, such as blue skin, switch this the other way.
If your video comes out garbled or striped, try the other format.
Video calls are encoded by the phone\'s own video chip instead of by Khandaq. That saves battery, but on some phones the picture breaks up.
How sharp your picture is in video calls. A sharper picture needs a faster connection.
With the phone\'s video chip, the picture is renewed bit by bit instead of all at once, which keeps video steadier on a weak connection.
Sends half as many frames per second, about 12 instead of 25: less smooth, but it uses less data.
Asks the camera for 15 frames per second. On some phones Khandaq may then close when the camera starts.
Khandaq connects only directly, never through a relay, so contacts on networks that block direct paths cannot be reached. Applies the next time Khandaq starts.
Your traffic goes through the Tor network, so contacts do not see your internet address. It needs the Orbot app, is slower, and applies the next time Khandaq starts.
Opens Khandaq after the phone restarts, on Android 9 and earlier. Android 10 and later do not allow it: open Khandaq once after a restart.
